mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 6 Series 635d engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 6 Series 635d engine replacement typically costs £1,800-£3,200 for a used M57D30 unit, £2,800-£4,800 for a reconditioned engine, and £4,000-£6,000 for a fully rebuilt engine with warranty. Supply & fit adds £780-£1,040 in specialist labour (12-16 hours). Used engines offer the lowest upfront cost with limited warranty; reconditioned engines sit in the mid-range with some new parts fitted; rebuilt engines are the most expensive but fully restored to factory spec with a 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 6 Series 635d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include metallic rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start, rough idling, engine misfires, and loss of low-end responsiveness. In advanced cases, the engine may struggle to start or show a timing-related fault code. If you hear a rattle, have it inspected immediately - a snapped chain can destroy the cylinder head and valves.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 6 Series 635d?

acceptedAnswer.text: With average values of £5,300-£6,500, a full rebuilt engine at £4,000-£6,000 represents a significant investment. However, if your 635d is in excellent condition with low mileage, a rebuilt engine can extend its life by 150,000+ miles - often cheaper than buying a replacement car of similar specification. For sub-£5,000 cars, consider a used engine or timing chain repair; for £5,000-£7,000 cars, a reconditioned engine is viable; for £7,000+ cars, a rebuilt engine with warranty makes strong financial sense.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 6 Series 635d engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 6 Series 635d engine replacement takes 2-4 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. The M57D30 is a straight-six with good engine bay access, but the job requires dropping the subframe and removing the gearbox. Most specialists offer collection/delivery options nationwide with same-day dispatch available for in-stock engines.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 635d and 630i engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 635d uses the 3.0L M57D30 twin-turbo diesel (286hp, 580Nm), while the 630i uses a 3.0L N52 or N53 naturally aspirated petrol (258-272hp). The 635d offers substantially more torque, better fuel economy (40.9mpg combined), but higher engine replacement costs due to the complexity of the twin-turbo diesel system.

The M57D30 is considered one of BMW's most reliable diesel engines, with many examples exceeding 200,000-300,000 miles when properly maintained. The key to longevity is regular oil changes with BMW LL-04 approved oil, avoiding short urban trips to prevent DPF clogging, and addressing timing chain rattles early.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 6 Series 635d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 635d joined the E63/E64 6 Series range in 2007 as the brand's first diesel-powered grand tourer, slotting above the 630i and alongside the V8 650i. Powered by BMW's acclaimed M57 twin-turbo straight-six, the 635d delivered V8-rivalling torque with diesel efficiency - and remained in production until the E63/E64 generation ended in 2010.

milestones.description: M57D30TU2 / M57D30T2, 3.0L twin-turbo diesel, 286hp, introduced as part of the 6 Series facelift (LCI)
2010 - M57D30 (306D5) 3.0L diesel, 286hp, fitted throughout E63 coupe and E64 convertible production
E63/E64 6 Series production ends; the 635d badge was not carried forward into the F06/F12/F13 generation

commonProblems.h2: BMW 6 Series 635d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 6 Series 635d is powered exclusively by the M57D30 family of 3.0-litre twin-turbo diesel engines - one of BMW's most robust diesel platforms, but not without its weaknesses. Rebuilt M57D30 engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded timing chain components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch - Why the BMW 6 Series 635d M57D30 Wears Prematurely
problems.typicalFailureMileage: 150,000-200,000+ miles (sooner with poor oil change history)
problems.rootCause: The M57's timing chain is front-mounted and generally durable, but chain guides and tensioners can wear over time, particularly when oil changes are stretched beyond BMW's recommended intervals. Chain elongation of 2%+ can cause rough idling, loss of responsiveness, and eventual catastrophic engine failure if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chains, guides, tensioners, sprockets; sump drop and timing cover removal required
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early before valve/piston damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if chain has snapped or caused collateral damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 6 Series 635d currently values between £4,600 and £8,900 depending on mileage, condition, and whether it's a coupe or convertible. With average private sale prices around £5,300-£6,500, a full rebuilt engine at £4,000-£6,000 represents 60-100% of the vehicle's value. For sub-£5,000 examples, a used engine or timing chain repair is usually more cost-effective. For £6,500+ examples in good condition, a rebuilt unit with warranty can be a sensible long-term investment.
problems.recommendation: If your 635d's timing chain is rattling but the engine hasn't skipped timing, the specialist chain replacement route (£1,200-£2,000) offers the best value - it addresses the failure point without the cost of a full engine swap. If the chain has snapped or you're experiencing loss of power, misfires, or metal in the oil, a rebuilt M57D30 engine is the safer bet.

problems.h4: DPF & EGR Clogging - Urban Driving Shortens M57D30 Life
problems.rootCause: The M57TU2 generation's DPF and EGR systems are sensitive to short journeys and stop-start driving. Without regular motorway runs to initiate passive DPF regeneration, the filter clogs, triggering warning lights, reduced power, and increased fuel consumption.
